prompt:
Our gaming platform is getting flooded with toxic player chat that bypasses simple word filters — people are using number substitutions, weird characters, and symbol tricks to evade detection. I need you to build a Node.js moderation pipeline that reads all the player comments from `platform/chat/incoming_comments.jsonl`, runs them through a robust content moderation check that can handle these evasion tricks (including the most aggressive obfuscation attempts), and outputs a file called `moderation_report.json` in the workspace root.

The report should contain ONLY the flagged/problematic comments (not clean ones). For each flagged comment, include the original entry data, a censored version of the text where profane words have their first letter preserved followed by asterisks (e.g., `f***` not `****`), and the list of detected words that triggered the flag.

Performance matters — use a batch processing approach rather than checking comments one by one.
